observations: Photo 0 shows the TV powered on, displaying the webOS home screen with various app icons including Netflix, YouTube, and LG Gallery+; a soundbar and a small black box (possibly a game console) are visible below.
Photo 1 shows the TV displaying a high-resolution aerial view of a tropical island with clear blue water.
The TV has a slim black bezel and is mounted on a white marble-patterned wall.
A silver analog clock is mounted on the wall above the TV.

claims.evidence: The webOS interface shown in photo 0 is exclusive to LG TVs.
The physical dimensions of the TV are not shown in the photos.
No model number is visible on the TV in either photo.
While the image in photo 1 is very clear, it does not confirm the specific resolution or panel technology.
The webOS interface in photo 0 confirms it is a smart TV.

risks.risk: The TV may not power on or may have a dead pixel.
risks.proof: A video showing the TV booting up and displaying a test pattern or a live video feed.

risks.risk: The actual screen size may be smaller than 86 inches.
risks.proof: A photo of the TV with a measuring tape across the screen or a reference object.

risks.risk: The TV may have a broken or missing remote control.
risks.proof: A photo of the remote control and a video of it being used to navigate the menu.

risks.risk: The TV may have a hardware defect or backlight failure.
risks.proof: A photo of the TV powered on in a dark room to check for uniform brightness.

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Photo of the TV with a measuring tape to confirm the screen size.
Video of the TV powered on and navigating the webOS menu.
Photo of the TV powered on in a dark room to check for backlight issues.
response.reason: What the item is shows, but not the model that sets its price: no photo shows it clearly enough to read. The shot asked for first would settle it.
